title: SRender: Boosting Neural Radiance Field Efficiency via Sensitivity-Aware Dynamic Precision Rendering
problem: Neural Radiance Fields require prohibitive computation and memory resources that prevent real-time deployment in VR/AR applications. Existing NeRF accelerators optimize only full-precision models, yielding unsatisfactory memory and computation savings.
motivation: Photo-realistic image and video generation via NeRF is impeded by high computational and memory demands, blocking deployment in real-time applications.
method: SRender identifies which rays (light paths used in rendering) and points (3D locations in the scene) matter most for image quality using a fast, approximate encoding method called low-precision hash encoding. It then devotes expensive, accurate high-precision computation to these important rays and points, while using cheaper low-precision approximations for the rest. The hardware is specifically designed for this: it includes a sensitivity prediction engine to identify importance, encoding engines optimized to reuse data in fast on-chip cache, and a recovery engine that converts computational savings into actual speedup.
key_novelty: Dynamically assigning different precision levels to individual rays and points based on how much each affects the final image enables efficient mixed-precision rendering.
contributions: Algorithm that dynamically configures precision of hash table and MLP based on per-ray and per-point sensitivity levels
Specialized hardware accelerator with sensitivity prediction engine and coarse-then-fine-grained encoding engines
Data reuse optimization on-chip to reduce off-chip memory bandwidth
Achieves 3.94x speedup over NeuRex and 34.06x over Jetson AGX Xavier with negligible quality loss

metrics.speedup: 3.94x over NeuRex, 34.06x over Jetson AGX Xavier GPU
